idiom_name: ViewModel + MutableStateFlow<UiState> + sealed Intent + reduce(state, intent)
implementation_notes: Kotlin/Android is where MVI became a mainstream recipe: a state holder (ViewModel) owns one MutableStateFlow<UiState>, user actions arrive as sealed interface Intent values through a single onIntent entry point, a pure reduce(state, intent) computes the next immutable data-class state, and the UI collects it with collectAsStateWithLifecycle while one-shot effects go through a SharedFlow or Channel. What replaces the classic MVI structure is the framework's own unidirectional-flow tooling - StateFlow is the conflated state stream, viewModelScope provides structured effect handling - which is why the classification is idiomatic rather than manual; libraries such as Orbit MVI, Mavericks or Circuit package the container and lifecycle/test tooling. Choose the hand-rolled form to stay dependency-free, the library when container, saved-state and test support are wanted.
pitfalls: StateFlow conflates equal consecutive values, so a state that should re-trigger work or a one-shot effect is silently dropped; model one-shot events separately (SharedFlow/Channel).
Writing to _state from several coroutines without a single reduce path interleaves transitions; funnel every change through update { reduce(it, intent) } on one dispatcher.
A ViewModel holding Context or View references outlives the screen and leaks; keep the state holder free of UI types and cancel work with viewModelScope.
Collecting the flow without the lifecycle (plain collect in an effect, collectAsState in older Compose) keeps updating backgrounded screens; use collectAsStateWithLifecycle or repeatOnLifecycle.

variants.name: Orbit MVI container (intent/reduce/postSideEffect) for Kotlin Multiplatform
variants.implementation_notes: Orbit MVI is a type-safe MVI framework for Kotlin Multiplatform and Android that packages the loop into an OrbitContainer: intent { reduce { state.copy(...) } } defines the transition, postSideEffect emits one-shot effects alongside the state stream, flows are collected lifecycle-safely, and the container exposes state/side-effect observers plus test utilities. Reach for it when the container, saved state, Compose binding and testing tooling are worth the dependency; the hand-rolled StateFlow variant reaches the same loop with framework primitives alone.
pitfalls: Side effects must go through postSideEffect, not into the state, or recomposition replays navigation/toasts.
The container's state flow is conflated like StateFlow; distinct one-shot events need the side-effect stream.
Reducers inside intent blocks must stay pure - blocking calls suspend the container's serialized intent processing.
